title: Keeping the prompt short, direct and free of contradictory instructions

videos.script: A prompt grows. Somebody sees one bad answer and adds a line. Nobody ever deletes one. {{title}} This lesson starts from a prompt after a few weeks of that. It is eighteen lines long, and it sends ninety-seven tokens more than the version it grew from, on every call. {{long}} Two of its lines disagree. One asks for a brief summary. The other, added later, asks for the problem in full detail. Nobody can obey both, so the model picks. {{contradiction}} On one message the brief line wins. On average the detailed one does. There is no rule you could write down. {{summary}} You will find mistakes like that with a linter, and see what a linter cannot see. {{lint}} Then you cut the prompt back to eight lines and measure the cut. The same twenty-one messages pass, not one result moves, and every call is ninety-seven tokens lighter. {{compare}} By the end you can say what each line of a prompt is for, or you delete it. {{close}}
